entries.why_wrong: A missing `default` isn't the issue here — every value 1 through 7 is already handled by an explicit case, so there's no unmatched input silently falling through the bottom. The real problem is fallthrough *between* the handled cases: case 5 runs into case 6 and 7 and gets its `count` overwritten to 2.

Changing `count` to a `double` wouldn't fix anything, since the function only ever needs to hold one of two distinct values (1 or 2) at a time, not a value in between. The bug is that fallthrough overwrites the weekday assignment before the function returns, not that `int` lacks enough precision.

Java's `switch` statement allows integer (and char/enum/String) case labels just fine — the numeric labels `1` through `7` here are perfectly legal and this code compiles. The actual defect is missing `break` statements causing case 5 to fall into case 6, not any restriction on label types.
